newsitem.title: JORDAN: Two Jordan banks in country's first bank merger.
newsitem.headline: Two Jordan banks in country's first bank merger.

text.p: Two Jordanian banks, National Bank and Business Bank, will formally approve on Saturday the first merger in the country's banking history, bankers said on Thursday.
The merger, with the new bank retaining the existing name of Jordan National Bank, will create Jordan's second largest bank in terms of capitalisation.
Its 42 million dinar ($59.3 million) capital is second to leading Arab Bank's 44 million dinar capital.

An extraordinary AGM meeting of the two banks' shareholders is expected to approve on Saturday the recommendations reached by a committee of the two banks, which finalised evaluation of assets, shareholders rights and stock evaluations.
"Effective Sunday 26, Business Bank will have ended as an independant bank and will be merged in Jordan National Bank," Abdul-Rahman Toukan, general manager of Jordan National Bank, told Reuters.
Toukan said that the merger will give the new entity more elbow room to expand in investment and commercial banking.
"Of course the larger capital will allow us to enter into more investment banking and comprehensive banking," he added.
Jordan National Bank, which has four Lebanon branches, one in Cyprus and five branches in Palestinian self-rule areas, also saw the merger allowing for expansion abroad, Toukan said.

The two banks' boards agreed to a merger last June and their shareholders have since given approval to proceed. Cross ownership of above 20 percent between their shareholders has aided the voluntary merger.
The committee's report put the total assets of the merged bank at 630 million dinars, which will put it fourth in rank among Jordan's 21 private banks after Arab bank, Housing Bank and Islamic Bank.
Non-combined assets of Jordan National Bank stand at 461.9 million dinars and Business Bank's at 167.1 million dinars, according to a copy of the report obtained by Reuters.
The new bank's shareholders rights will stand at 67.8 million dinars with total deposits of 448.4 million dinars and 319.5 million dinars of loans.

Under the asset evaluation, existing Jordan National Bank shareholders will own nearly 85 percent of the new merged bank's capital or 36 million dinars. They will get an extra one and a quarter shares for every existing share they hold.
Business Bank shareholders will get one new share for every share in their dissolved bank, only 15 percent of the combined capital which reflects dominance of their larger partner.
